overview: BlackRock is the world's largest asset manager, with record assets under management (AUM) of approximately $15.5 trillion as of September 30, 2026, serving institutional, intermediary, and individual investors in more than 100 countries. The firm earns the large majority of its revenue from fees calculated as a percentage of AUM across active, index (iShares ETFs), cash management, and a rapidly expanding private-markets platform, and separately sells its Aladdin risk-management/portfolio technology as enterprise subscription software to third-party institutions. Following the 2024-2025 acquisitions of Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), Preqin, and HPS Investment Partners, BlackRock has repositioned itself as an integrated public-private markets and technology platform, with management targeting technology and private markets combined to reach 30%+ of firm revenue by 2030.

business_model.summary: BlackRock earns the large majority of revenue from base investment advisory and administration fees calculated as a percentage of AUM, supplemented by securities lending revenue, performance fees (increasingly weighted to private markets/alternatives), technology services/subscription revenue (Aladdin), distribution fees, and advisory/other revenue. Nine-months-2026 revenue was $21.53 billion, up from $17.21 billion in the prior-year period (+25% YoY), reflecting market appreciation, record net inflows, and the first full annualized quarters of consolidated HPS and Preqin revenue. Q3 2026 revenue was $7.75 billion (+19% YoY), with technology services and subscription revenue of $588 million (+14% YoY) and GAAP diluted EPS of $10.57 (+25% YoY); adjusted EPS of $15.93 beat consensus of ~$14.15-14.32. Base fees are largely recurring (tied to AUM levels, which move with markets and net flows) while performance fees and technology ACV bookings add a more volatile, higher-margin overlay; management flagged that Q3 2026's performance-fee strength was driven materially by one hedge fund with a Q3-ending annual period and should not be extrapolated every quarter.

revenue_streams.name: Base fees & securities lending (long-term products + cash mgmt)

business_model.customer_type: Predominantly B2B/institutional (pension funds, insurers, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, corporations, banks, financial advisors/wirehouses) with a large retail/individual investor base reached via ETFs (iShares), mutual funds, and retirement platforms; Aladdin is sold B2B to other asset managers, banks and insurers as enterprise software
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas is the largest revenue and AUM base, with significant and growing EMEA and Asia-Pacific operations; AUM and flows are increasingly global, with private markets and Aladdin sold internationally

competitive_position.market_position: World's largest asset manager by AUM (~$15.5T, September 2026); dominant #1 in global ETFs through iShares as part of the 'Big Three' index-fund complex alongside Vanguard and State Street, though that trio's collective share of new inflows has eroded from its historical peak as low-cost and thematic entrants (Vanguard, JPMorgan, Schwab, Dimensional) chip away at flows. In technology, Aladdin is the leading enterprise risk-management/portfolio platform used by hundreds of institutions overseeing tens of trillions in assets. Following GIP/Preqin/HPS, BlackRock has rapidly become a top-tier player in private credit and infrastructure, including a role as co-founder (with Microsoft, MGX and Nvidia) of the Global AI Infrastructure Investment Partnership targeting up to $100 billion of AI data-center and power investment, though BlackRock remains smaller than pure-play alternatives leaders (Blackstone, Apollo, KKR, Ares) in those niches.

moat_factors.description: AUM of ~$15.5T generates enormous operating leverage; BlackRock can run index and ETF products at industry-low expense ratios while maintaining a 45%+ adjusted operating margin, a bar smaller managers struggle to match.

Aladdin is deeply embedded in clients' front-to-back office workflows (risk, trading, portfolio construction); once integrated it creates high switching costs and recurring, sticky, high-margin subscription revenue (~$588M quarterly, +14% YoY in Q3 2026) that also functions as a channel to cross-sell BlackRock's own investment products.
The BlackRock/iShares brand is a default choice for advisors and institutions; extensive distribution relationships with wirehouses, RIAs, banks, and retirement platforms lock in flows.

Uniquely broad shelf spanning index, active, ETFs, cash management, and now (via GIP/HPS/Preqin) private equity, infrastructure, and private credit, allowing BlackRock to offer integrated public-private portfolio solutions few competitors can match end-to-end.

Preqin's private-markets data combined with Aladdin/eFront gives BlackRock a differentiated data moat in the historically opaque private-markets space, aiding both internal underwriting and third-party data-subscription sales.

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on capital markets levels — AUM and fee revenue are directly exposed to equity/bond market drawdowns, which BlackRock cannot control
Fee compression in commoditized index/ETF products continues as Vanguard and others compete aggressively on price
Integration risk and goodwill/intangible exposure from three large, near-simultaneous acquisitions (GIP, Preqin, HPS) closed within an 18-month window
Political/ESG backlash has led several US states to divest pension assets from BlackRock, a reputational and AUM headwind concentrated in red-state public funds

Alternatives/private-markets business still smaller than pure-play leaders (Blackstone, Apollo, KKR) despite the recent buildout, and higher fee private-market products carry more competitive and vintage-timing risk than passive index funds

Performance-fee quality: Q3 2026's outsized performance-fee contribution was concentrated in a single hedge fund with a Q3 annual period, underscoring the lumpy, non-recurring nature of this growing revenue line

growth_drivers: Private markets buildout: GIP (infrastructure, closed Oct 2024), Preqin (private-markets data, closed 2025) and HPS Investment Partners (private credit, ~$12B all-equity deal, closed July 1, 2025) together create an integrated private-credit franchise with roughly $220B+ in client assets; management targets technology and private markets combined reaching 30%+ of firm revenue by 2030 and expects the private credit market to more than double to $4.5 trillion by 2030

AI infrastructure investing: BlackRock, GIP, Microsoft, MGX and Nvidia co-founded the Global AI Infrastructure Investment Partnership (GAIIP), aiming to mobilize up to $100 billion for AI data centers and supporting power infrastructure, extending BlackRock's infrastructure franchise into the AI capex buildout

Aladdin/technology services scaling: technology services and subscription revenue continues double-digit growth (+14% YoY in Q3 2026), extending Aladdin into private markets via eFront and Preqin integration

iShares/ETF secular growth: continued global shift from active to passive and from mutual funds to ETFs, plus growing adoption of active and fixed-income ETFs, model portfolios, and a newly introduced 40 Act 2a-7 money market fund aligned with GENIUS Act stablecoin-reserve rules

Retirement/401(k) private-markets expansion: BlackRock is building proprietary LifePath target-date funds with private-asset allocations and partnering with platforms like Great Gray Trust to embed private equity/credit into defined-contribution plans, targeting a large, largely untapped US retirement AUM pool

Record organic growth and net inflows: Q3 2026 net inflows of $205.5 billion and trailing-twelve-month inflows of roughly $869 billion, broad-based across ETFs, private markets, active fixed income, and systematic equity
Continued capital return: share buyback guidance of at least $550 million per quarter alongside a growing dividend (quarterly dividend of $5.73, ~2.1% yield)

business.description: The large majority of revenue is a percentage of AUM; a sustained equity/bond market decline mechanically reduces base fees and performance fees, independent of net flows.
Intense price competition, especially from Vanguard, continues to compress expense ratios on commoditized ETF and index products, requiring continued AUM growth just to hold fee revenue flat.

Founder and Chairman/CEO Larry Fink (73) remains the dominant public face and strategic architect of BlackRock; he has publicly said finding a successor to himself and President Rob Kapito is his top priority, but no named successor has emerged as of November 2026 following the 2025 departure of a leading internal contender, Mark Wiedman. An eventual leadership transition carries execution and market-perception risk.

Multiple US states have divested billions in pension assets from BlackRock over ESG-related political controversy; the firm has publicly stepped back from ESG branding, which itself carries reputational risk with the opposite constituency (institutional/European clients favoring ESG mandates).

financial.description: GIP, Preqin, and HPS were all acquired within an ~18-month window (2024-2025), adding significant goodwill/intangibles and integration complexity; failure to realize projected synergies or retain key private-markets investment talent would pressure returns on the ~$15B+ combined deal value.
Management guides to mid-single-digit percentage growth in full-year G&A after annualizing HPS and Preqin, a cost headwind that must be offset by revenue synergies to sustain margin expansion.

Performance fees (~7% of revenue, increasingly weighted to private markets/alternatives) are inherently lumpy and tied to fund vintage performance and realization timing; Q3 2026's spike was concentrated in a single hedge fund with a Q3 annual period.

regulatory.description: BlackRock's scale (Aladdin's use across trillions of third-party assets plus its own ~$15.5T AUM) keeps alive periodic regulatory discussion of designating large asset managers as systemically important, which could bring bank-like capital and oversight requirements.
Operating in 100+ countries exposes BlackRock to a patchwork of securities, fiduciary, data-privacy, and antitrust regulation; violations can trigger fines, license suspension, or reputational harm.

Expanding private assets into 401(k)/target-date funds depends on continued regulatory support (e.g., DOL guidance); a change in the political/regulatory stance toward private assets in retirement plans could slow this growth driver.
BlackRock's new GENIUS Act-aligned money market fund ties a product line to an evolving stablecoin/digital-asset regulatory framework whose implementation details are still being finalized.

macro.risk: Interest rate and credit cycle exposure
macro.description: Cash management AUM/fees and the newly expanded private-credit book (via HPS) are sensitive to interest-rate levels and credit-cycle conditions; a sharp downturn could pressure private-credit valuations and fundraising.
A global recession or sustained bear market would reduce AUM, net flows, and performance fees simultaneously, the single largest swing factor for earnings.

BlackRock's growing exposure to AI data-center and power infrastructure investment (via GIP and GAIIP) ties a portion of future private-markets fundraising and returns to the durability of the current AI capex boom; a slowdown or re-pricing of AI infrastructure demand would be a new cyclical exposure.
International AUM and revenue are subject to translation effects from US dollar movements.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global asset management continues to consolidate around scale players; passive/ETF adoption keeps growing, private credit is projected by BlackRock to more than double to $4.5 trillion by 2030, and asset managers are racing to embed private markets into retail/retirement channels. A large pool of capital, including BlackRock's own, is being directed toward AI data-center and power infrastructure. Technology/analytics (Aladdin-like platforms) are viewed as a structurally faster-growing, higher-margin adjacent business.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — revenue and profitability are directly linked to global capital markets levels (equity and bond values) and net flows, both of which are cyclical and sentiment-driven, though the diversified multi-asset-class, multi-geography platform and recurring technology subscription revenue reduce volatility versus a single-strategy manager.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — affects cash management fee economics, fixed income AUM valuations, and the economics of the newly acquired private-credit (HPS) platform; also an indirect driver of overall risk appetite and equity/bond valuations that determine AUM.

recent_developments.event: Q3 2026 earnings reported: record AUM of approximately $15.5 trillion (+15% YoY); revenue of $7.75B (+19% YoY) versus ~$7.42B consensus; Q3 net inflows of $205.5B, trailing-twelve-month inflows of ~$869B; GAAP diluted EPS of $10.57 (+25% YoY); adjusted EPS of $15.93 beat the ~$14.15-14.32 consensus; management flagged that a large share of the performance-fee beat came from one hedge fund with a Q3-ending annual period, cautioning against extrapolating it.

Mixed analyst reaction to Q3 results despite the beat — shares fell ~1.5% on the print even as JPMorgan raised its price target to $1,449 (overweight) and consensus average target sat near $1,312, while Evercore ISI had cut its target to $1,207 in September; dividend of $5.73/quarter ($22.92 annualized, ~2.1% yield) was maintained.

BlackRock introduced a new 40 Act 2a-7 money market fund structured to align with the GENIUS Act's stablecoin-reserve framework, positioning the firm in the evolving digital-asset/stablecoin infrastructure space.

CEO Larry Fink warned at the Canada Investment Summit that public pushback against AI infrastructure build-out risks making the technology the 'domain of large firms,' limiting broader access — part of continued public commentary on AI's economic impact and BlackRock's own growing role as an AI-infrastructure investor via GIP.

BlackRock, GIP, Microsoft, MGX and Nvidia advanced the Global AI Infrastructure Investment Partnership (GAIIP), targeting up to $100 billion in AI data-center and power-infrastructure investment, with most capital directed to the US.

Q2 2026 earnings reported: record AUM of $15.3 trillion; revenue of $7.08B (+31% YoY); adjusted operating margin of 46.5% (+260bps YoY, highest in nearly five years); record H1 2026 net inflows of $321B including $192B in Q2 alone.

Completed the ~$12 billion all-equity acquisition of HPS Investment Partners, creating an integrated private-credit franchise with roughly $220 billion in client assets and materially expanding BlackRock's alternatives platform.
Completed the acquisition of Preqin, a leading independent private-markets data provider, for approximately $3.2 billion in cash, to be integrated with Aladdin/eFront.

Continued embedding private assets into US retirement/401(k) plans, including a custom glidepath partnership with Great Gray Trust Company incorporating private equity and private credit into a target-date fund.

Technology services and subscription revenue grew 14% YoY in Q3 2026 to $588M, consistent with the double-digit growth trend seen earlier in 2026.

guidance.management_commentary: On the Q3 2026 call, management highlighted record AUM (~$15.5T), record quarterly net inflows ($205.5B), and an EPS beat as continued validation of the integrated public-private markets and technology strategy built via GIP, Preqin, and HPS, while also flagging the AI-infrastructure investment opportunity through GAIIP (with Microsoft, MGX, and Nvidia) as a new, large-scale avenue for the private-markets platform. Management reiterated confidence in sustained double-digit organic growth, continued margin expansion, and the medium-term target of technology plus private markets reaching over 30% of firm revenue by 2030, while cautioning investors not to extrapolate the unusually large Q3 performance-fee contribution, which was concentrated in a single fund's annual crystallization period.

bull_case: Record scale and momentum: ~$15.5 trillion in AUM with record quarterly net inflows ($205.5B in Q3 2026, ~$869B TTM) demonstrate the platform is compounding faster than pre-acquisition trends

Successful pivot into higher-margin, faster-growing private markets and technology: GIP, Preqin, and HPS collectively build an integrated private-credit and infrastructure franchise (~$220B+ client assets) alongside Aladdin's double-digit growing technology subscription revenue, with management targeting >30% of revenue from technology + private markets by 2030

New AI-infrastructure growth vector: co-founding the Global AI Infrastructure Investment Partnership with Microsoft, MGX, and Nvidia gives BlackRock/GIP a seat at the center of the AI data-center and power buildout, a potentially multi-decade capital deployment opportunity
Margin expansion story remains intact: adjusted operating margin of 46.5% in Q2 2026 (highest in nearly five years) with management stating this is not a ceiling as newly-scaled businesses mature
Strong capital returns: buyback guidance of at least $550M/quarter plus a growing dividend (~2.1% yield), funded by robust free cash flow generation even through a period of heavy M&A integration
bear_case: Heavy dependence on capital markets levels: the vast majority of revenue is AUM-based; a sustained equity/bond bear market would mechanically compress base fees, performance fees, and overall earnings, a risk management cannot fully offset with organic growth alone

Performance-fee quality concerns: Q3 2026's earnings beat was flattered by an unusually large, one-off performance fee from a single hedge fund, raising the bar for Q4 2026 and beyond and highlighting the lumpiness underlying the headline EPS growth

Integration risk from three large, near-simultaneous acquisitions: GIP, Preqin, and HPS were all completed within roughly 18 months; realizing promised synergies and retaining key private-credit/infrastructure talent remain unproven over a full multi-year cycle, and the stock fell on the Q3 2026 print despite the beat, suggesting the market is parsing underlying quality rather than headline numbers

Succession uncertainty: Larry Fink (73) has called finding his and President Rob Kapito's successors his top priority, but no named heir has emerged as of November 2026 after a leading internal candidate departed in 2025, leaving a key-person overhang

Valuation and expectations risk: analyst price targets ranging roughly $1,207-$1,531 (consensus near $1,300-1,450) already embed continued record inflows and margin expansion; any disappointment in flows, AI-infrastructure fundraising, or integration costs could compress the multiple given how much good news is already priced in

New AI-infrastructure concentration: growing capital commitments to data-center/power investing via GAIIP tie a portion of future private-markets returns to the durability of the current AI capex cycle, a relatively untested and potentially crowded trade
